claims.text: Near-equiatomic FeCoNi is a single-phase FCC alloy with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
Near-equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetic behavior.
Adding a near-equiatomic amount of Al to FeCoNi produces a FeCoNiAl high-entropy alloy with configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Al incorporation into FeCoNi promotes B2 ordering.
FeCoNiAl can be processed into a state with partial B2 ordering.
Al incorporation creates local lattice distortions in FeCoNiAl.
Partial B2 ordering and local lattice distortions increase local magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Partial B2 ordering and local lattice distortions create effective domain-wall pinning sites.
The proposed pinning sites restrict domain-wall motion and thereby increase coercivity.
FeCoNiAl will have approximately 50–200% greater coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
FeCoNiAl will largely preserve the high saturation magnetization of FeCoNi.
Annealing temperature can alter the ordered and disordered phase constitution of FeCoNiAl.
High-temperature FeCoNiAl can form a single ordered B2 phase, whereas lower annealing temperatures can produce an ordered-B2 plus disordered-BCC mixture.
The proposed coercivity enhancement occurs only near equiatomic composition and under heat treatments favoring partial B2 ordering.
Departures from the proposed Al range or overly aggressive annealing can cause complete ordering or phase separation.
Complete ordering or phase separation will undermine the coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: The mechanism describes B2 ordering 'within the FCC matrix' while the conditions seek partial B2 ordering rather than phase separation. B2 is an ordered BCC-derived structure, so retaining an FCC matrix with B2 regions implies distinct phases rather than a simple partially ordered FCC state.
